title: Tesla-SpaceX Merger Could Face The Biggest Regulatory Risk In China, BofA Warns

Tesla-SpaceX Merger Could Face The Biggest Regulatory Risk In China, BofA Warns
Arnab Paul

TSLA
SPCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The merger could raise national security concerns and complicate regulatory approval in China, BofA said.

The Shanghai factory has an installed annual production capacity exceeding 950,000 vehicles annually.

BofA said a potential merger would involve SpaceX acquiring the EV maker through an all-stock deal.

A potential merger between Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) could face its biggest regulatory challenge in China, Bank of America reportedly said on Friday, citing Tesla's dependence on its Shanghai factory and SpaceX's ties to the U.S. defense industry.

SPCX shares were down more than 5% at the time of writing, while TSLA stock fell 1.8%.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Why Is China A Major Concern?

According to Investing.com, BofA said Tesla's Shanghai plant, which accounts for roughly half its global vehicle production for both domestic and overseas markets, would come under the ownership of a major U.S. defense contractor if the companies merged.

That could raise national security concerns and complicate regulatory approval in China. According to Tesla, the Shanghai factory has an installed annual production capacity exceeding 950,000 vehicles annually.

In an interview with CNBC last week, former Tesla board member Steve Westly highlighted similar concerns over the merger, citing regulatory challenges and national security risks.

What Would A Potential Merger Look Like?

BofA said a potential merger would involve SpaceX acquiring the EV maker through an all-stock deal. "The key question, in our view, is whether TSLA's special committee can negotiate a premium, which we think is likely given Tesla's core auto momentum and robotaxi inflection," BofA reportedly said.

The firm maintained its 'Buy' rating and $460 price target on Tesla.

Earlier this month, Musk confirmed that both companies had formed independent committees to explore a merger, but emphasized that a deal remains uncertain.

Retail Remains Bearish On TSLA, SPCX

Retail sentiment surrounding both TSLA and SPCX on Stocktwits trended in the 'bearish' zone over the past 24 hours.

One user believes Tesla's high valuation will not hold, with a deal likely to value Tesla much lower.

TSLA shares are down 9% so far in 2026 while a sharp sell-off this month has brought SPCX stock close to its IPO price of $135.

title: Tesla Could Be About to Unlock a Brand-New Revenue Stream. Time to Buy the Stock?
detail:
Tesla Could Be About to Unlock a Brand-New Revenue Stream. Time to Buy the Stock?
Prosper Junior Bakiny, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 1:09 PM EDT 5 min read
TSLA
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) has been a pioneer in the electric vehicle (EV) market, and the company still generates the lion's share of its revenue from this segment. However, the EV landscape has been somewhat uncertain in recent years, affecting Tesla's financial results. Thankfully, Tesla has several attractive potential growth opportunities, and the company could unlock a new revenue stream by the end of the year. Here's what investors need to know.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Could the Cybercab soon hit the proverbial shelves?

In September, Tesla launched the Cybercab, an autonomous vehicle with two seats, no steering wheel, no pedals, and no mirrors. The Cybercab is an important piece in Tesla's robotaxi ambition.

The vehicle is likely cheaper to manufacture than the Model Y and could generate sales over its entire useful life. The economics of Tesla's robotaxi business could be much more profitable than its consumer EV sales. Here is why.

Tesla makes a significant amount of money every time it sells an EV, but annual sales after that are fairly modest -- they come from the $99 per month subscription to the company's Full Self-Driving (FSD) software. But Cybercabs, if used extensively, could generate thousands of dollars in revenue each year.

Suppose each Cybercab accommodates 10 rides per day at an average price of $15 -- that's $150 every day, or $54,750 per year. And let's assume a 10-year useful life; that's $547,500 over the car's life. That's far more in sales than what Tesla can make from its most popular car, the Model Y, over its entire useful life.

Our assumptions might turn out to be wrong, but the potential for Tesla's robotaxi fleet is there, and it helps explain why so many investors are excited about the company's future. However, Tesla has another plan in mind. In addition to running its own fleet of Cybercabs, the company wants to sell them to consumers and allow them to operate their own fleets.

It intends to start selling the Cybercab by year-end. Tesla could then generate revenue from commissions on every ride booked through its network, or perhaps from FSD subscription fees, or maybe from repair and maintenance, although the company has not indicated that yet.

Whatever the case may be, selling Cybercabs would allow the company to combine one benefit of its EV business -- upfront revenue from the sale of a car -- with the perks of its robotaxi fleet. There is also the possibility that Tesla will eventually sell its Cybercab to large corporations for a variety of purposes, such as delivering packages.

title: Micron Became One of the 10 Biggest Holdings in S&P 500 Index Funds. What Does That Mean for the Stock?
detail:
Micron Became One of the 10 Biggest Holdings in S&P 500 Index Funds. What Does That Mean for the Stock?
00:00 / 00:00
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 1:01 PM EDT 5 min read
MU
VOO
TSLA
NVDA
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Memory maker Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) now ranks among the biggest companies in the stock market. At the end of September, it was the ninth-largest holding in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT:VOO), making up 1.82% of the fund.

This put it above Tesla, at 1.52%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Funds made to track the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) hold the same stocks at around the same weights, so Micron's place shows up in all of them. The whole Vanguard fund, which has about $1.7 trillion in the ETF and its other share classes, owned about 29.7 million Micron shares on Sept. 30, or around 2.6% of the company.

The rise has been quick. Micron's market value passed $1 trillion for the first time on May 26, and the stock has more than quadrupled in the last year. But shares are also down about 8% since Sept. 30, to roughly $983 as I write. I think the weight itself matters less for the stock than it may seem.

Image source: Getty Images.

The weight follows the price

The S&P 500 is weighted by float-adjusted market value. That means S&P Dow Jones Indices counts the market value of each company's shares that are available to public investors, and a stock's weight is its share of that total.

Put another way, Micron's spot in the top 10 came from its stock price, which climbed much faster than the rest of the market.

That also explains how Micron passed Tesla. At the end of September, Tesla's shares were worth around $1.4 trillion all told, more than Micron's $1.2 trillion or so.

But Micron had the higher weight, because a far larger chunk of Tesla's stock falls outside what the index counts as available to the public.

The weight moves both ways, too. With Micron's shares down since Sept. 30, its weight in the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust was 1.54% on Oct. 26. That was below Tesla's 1.67%, and it put Micron just outside the top 10 that day.

Does the top 10 draw in more buyers?

Not on its own. After all, an index fund already holds every stock in proportion to its weight, so when Micron's price rises, the fund's stake gains value without the fund buying more shares.

Nothing new happens the day a stock moves from 11th place to ninth.

What does change is where new money goes. At a weight of around 1.6%, every $1,000 investors put into an S&P 500 fund now sends about $16 into Micron, much more than a year ago.

Of course, it works the other way, too. When money leaves these funds, their Micron holdings shrink in the same proportion. Index ownership hasn't kept the stock from sharp swings. Micron fell 6% on Oct. 22 alone, and it's about 19% under its record close, $1,213.56 on June 25.

Memory prices still matter most

Micron's stock, and its weight with it, climbed mostly because its earnings did, with demand from AI projects boosting its memory sales.

A year ago, the memory maker's quarterly revenue was $11.3 billion. Micron's fiscal 2026 ended on Sept. 3, and revenue in that year's last quarter reached $54.2 billion, up 379% year over year and 31% above the fiscal third quarter's $41.5 billion.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, management expects around $61.5 billion. Yes, that'd set another record. But it implies sequential growth of around 13%, a slowdown from the 31% rate of the last quarter.

Earnings per share for fiscal 2026 came to $74.33, up around 880% from $7.59 in fiscal 2025.

At around $983, the stock trades at about 13 times earnings, about half the 24.7 times earnings Vanguard listed for its S&P 500 fund at the end of September. Investors are paying much less for every dollar of Micron's profit than for the index overall, probably because memory prices have long moved in cycles.

For anyone who holds an S&P 500 fund, the top-10 spot mainly means Micron's swings show up more. A 10% fall in Micron would knock around 0.16% off the fund.

Does the top-10 spot change anything for the stock, then? Not much by itself. The index just gives Micron more weight when the stock beats the market and less when it trails. What moves the price is still memory demand.

And the company is still growing. At about 13 times earnings, I'd consider buying the shares. But anyone who holds an S&P 500 fund already has some Micron, and a fall in memory prices could hurt both.

title: What Just Happened To Alnylam Stock?
detail:

Alnylam Pharmaceuticals (ALNY) stock fell 25.1% on Thursday, October 29, 2026, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.3%. The drop came on the day Alnylam reported third-quarter results that beat revenue estimates and hosted its earnings call. So what did management say about demand for its drugs?

Alnylam Is Not Yet Satisfied With Demand Growth

During the call, management said it is "not yet satisfied with the underlying demand growth" it has seen, adding that this is reflected in its outlook for the full year. The company expects TTR product sales, which come from its transthyretin drugs including AMVUTTRA, to land at the low end of its $4.2 billion to $4.5 billion range.

A company's own targets hold only if demand for its main product grows fast enough. For example, Tesla has over 1.7 million paid FSD customers, only half of them on subscriptions, far short of the 10 million subscriptions that Musk's pay package requires. Read Trefis Big Story: Musk's Massive Marketing Miss Cost $10 Trillion.

Alnylam beat revenue estimates for the quarter, reporting $1.46 billion against an estimate of $1.43 billion. A one-time item lifted reported profit: GAAP net income of $2.2 billion included a non-cash tax benefit of about $1.9 billion, management said. Product revenue grew 52% from a year earlier to about $1.3 billion, led by AMVUTTRA.

Management also said that turning new prescribers into patient starts is taking longer than it had hoped, because many newer physicians have fewer cardiomyopathy patients and less understanding of the disease. Furthermore, Alnylam will issue its 2027 product revenue guidance alongside its fourth-quarter results in mid-February, rather than at the JPMorgan conference as in past years.

Did Other Drug Stocks Fall With Alnylam?

No. XLV, the SPDR fund for the health care sector, rose 2.4% during the same session, and four of the five companies on Alnylam's peer list advanced. Gilead Sciences gained 4.0%, while Ionis Pharmaceuticals, the one peer that fell, lost 1.1%.

The wider market was weaker, with the Nasdaq Composite index down 1.4%, but that index drop was a small fraction of Alnylam's. The stock fell on its own, not alongside its group.

Where Does Alnylam Stock Stand Now?

While a fall this large is rare for Alnylam, it is the second in three months. In the 365 days before this session, the stock recorded one other fall at least this large, a 28.3% drop on July 30, 2026.

Over the past twelve months Alnylam has lost 63.9%, compared with a 13.3% gain for the S&P 500. Its $174.00 close on October 29 marked its lowest finish in that year, while its highest close was $481.59 on October 29, 2025. Over the past six months alone, the stock is down 43.8%.

Alnylam is expected to report its fourth-quarter 2026 results in February 2027, and full-year TTR product sales are the measure to watch.

Rivian Automotive (RIVN) was in the spotlight Friday as Wall Street reacted to the EV maker's third-quarter earnings beat and positive commentary on the R2 electric SUV.

RIVN shares were up 5.6% at the time of writing, tracking their biggest single-day gains in more than two months.

Jefferies Sees Product Void Between Tesla And Ford

Jefferies analyst Philippe Houchois upgraded Rivian to 'Buy' from 'Hold,' and maintained a $17 price target, according to The Fly. This implies roughly 45% upside from current levels. Houchois expects Rivian's R2 to benefit as U.S. electric vehicle demand begins to stabilize.

The analyst highlighted a "relatively unique position and product void" in the $45,000- $55,000 price range, between 'commoditizing' Tesla models and Ford's upcoming electric vehicle based on its Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform. However, the new EV platform may not see a significant production ramp until late 2027.

The analyst believes Rivian's roughly 30% stock correction over the past three months presents an attractive entry point as the company expands production and explores opportunities to license its autonomous driving technology. RIVN shares hit a high of $20.2 in July before sliding to below $12.

Rivian Raises Full Year 2026 Deliveries Guidance

On Thursday, Rivian reported 38% growth in Q3 revenue to $2.16 billion, while its adjusted loss narrowed to $0.48 per share. It updated its adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) outlook to a loss of $1.75 billion to $1.85 billion, a $100 million improvement at the midpoint, and lowered capital expenditure guidance to $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion.

CEO RJ Scaringe said the R2, which began deliveries in June, has already become Rivian's best-selling vehicle, outselling both its R1 models and electric delivery vans. The automaker has started a second R2 production shift at its Illinois factory, with more affordable versions expected to arrive through late 2026 and 2027.

Rivian also raised its full-year 2026 delivery forecast to 67,000–70,000 vehicles from 65,000–70,000 previously.

title: Jim Cramer has a new way of thinking about the biggest tech stocks
detail:
Jim Cramer has a new way of thinking about the biggest tech stocks

Some companies are so big that they stop behaving like ordinary stocks. That's the case Jim Cramer made on October 28, telling "Mad Money" viewers that a small club of tech giants has grown so powerful its reach now extends far beyond share prices.

He picked a telling night to say it.

Oil prices were climbing on renewed worries about the conflict with Iran, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warned that inflation was still elevated, and two of the biggest names in tech reported results that sent their shares in opposite directions.

Cramer's argument is that these companies can ride out rough seas better than most. He just isn't claiming they're unsinkable.

Cramer's 'nation states' and their aircraft carriers

Cramer listed 10 companies that fit his description: Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Meta Platforms (META), Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA), Tesla (TSLA), SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI.

He likened them to "nation states," pointing to their dominant market positions, their ability to churn out big profits and their willingness to pour money into new technology.

"Their heft is so extraordinary that 'Mad Money' cannot go without covering them," he said.

Also read: What Jim Cramer is watching as Anthropic heads to Nasdaq

The list stretches beyond the usual Magnificent Seven. Two of its members, Anthropic and OpenAI, still aren't publicly traded, though that's starting to change. Anthropic filed to go public on October 26 and plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

Their weight in the market is hard to overstate. The Magnificent Seven alone made up about 33.7% of the S&P 500 earlier this year, up from 12.5% a decade ago, TheStreet reported. When those stocks move, the whole index tends to follow.

Still, Cramer was careful not to call them bulletproof. He compared the group to aircraft carriers, which handle storms better than smaller boats but can still be pushed around by strong economic currents. Cramer's Charitable Trust, the portfolio run by CNBC's Investing Club, owns shares of six of the companies on his list.

Microsoft makes Cramer's case

Microsoft gave him his best example. The software giant reported revenue of $92.3 billion for its fiscal first quarter, up 19% from a year earlier, with its Azure cloud business growing 48%. Net income jumped 32% to $36.6 billion.

Investors liked what they saw. Shares climbed about 4% after hours as earnings and revenue topped estimates, and capital spending, including finance leases, came in at $45.2 billion, below what analysts had expected.

The 2030 numbers are interim milestones along that five-year path, and you should treat them as illustrative. If you hold the full five years, the model's central scenario raises the $1,000 to $1,269.40, a 26.94% total return, or 4.89% a year.
